label: intake form
description:
The intake form, filled in by two hands in two pens. Under what brought you here, Mom has written that Wren has been so good, honestly no trouble at all. Dad has written that she is a good little trooper.

Under changes in the family, both of them have ticked the box for separation.

label: school referral
description:
A letter on school letterhead, from Ms. Okafor. She writes that Wren used to share news every morning and lately just says pass. At lunch Wren sorts the class library into piles by color.

She adds that Wren is kind to everyone and has never once been a problem.

label: notes from week one
description: Your own notes, in your small square writing. Wren stayed by the door for ten minutes, holding the rabbit by one ear. She lined her shoes up. She told you her name and the day of the week, and nothing else.

label: notes from last week
description:
Last week. Wren built a tower of blocks without a word, knocked it down, and put every block back in the bin. She counted under her breath, and then stopped herself.

Underlined in pencil. Did not name the move. W. left the table when I said "two houses."

label: family schedule
description:
A typed page. Weekdays are at Mom's. Tuesday nights are at Dad's, and every second weekend. Thursday is a Mom day.

In the margin, in Dr. Bell's green ink. Both parents attentive. Child very tidy. Go slowly.

label: The Bird Who Carried Her Nest
aliases: the bird who carried her nest
description: A thin picture book. On the cover, a round brown bird holds a nest in both wings, with a tree on either side of her.

label: Bear Counts to Ten
description: A fat, cheerful picture book. On the cover, a bear holds one paw up, and ten red balloons float over his head.

label: Two Houses for Fox
description: A picture book with a fox standing between two small houses. A sticker on the spine reads Changing Families.

label: clementine and crackers
description: A clementine and four square crackers on a paper napkin.

label: notes from today
description: Session three. Dad dropped her off, and W. noticed before I did. She sorted the animals and counted. She kept the bag close, and I did not ask about it. We did not get far. Next time, the bins first, and no hurry about the book.

label: notes from today
description: Session three. W. told me some of what she keeps in the bag, and some of what she does at night so that the days stay straight. She said it to Rabbit first. Next time, no questions. Let her bring it.

label: notes from today
description: Session three. She showed me the handle. It was Mom's cup, and she was making tea, and she carried it with both hands. She thinks the shouting and the two houses came after it. I did not tell her it was not her fault. She will need to hear that from someone she has not been waiting to hear it from. Next session, the bins, and whatever she brings.
